nodes.norm_label: explicit viewport sizing to force responsive breakpoints

nodes.label: Readiness-wait convention (data-ready / data-draggable polling before interacting)
nodes.norm_label: readiness-wait convention (data-ready / data-draggable polling before interacting)

nodes.label: BlazorAppFixture
nodes.rationale: Blazor WebAssembly needs framework files served over real HTTP, so WebApplicationFactory cannot be used; the demo app is published (not `dotnet run`) so wwwroot/_framework sits next to the entry assembly for MapStaticAssets to serve the WASM runtime, and the publish dir is cleared first because `dotnet publish -o` does not prune stale fingerprinted asset bundles.

nodes.label: VetoPageTest
nodes.rationale: Waits for data-ready="true" on the page root rather than network idle, because prerendered HTML is present and inert before Blazor WebAssembly interactivity takes over.

nodes.label: Table not yet following component contract
nodes.norm_label: table not yet following component contract

nodes.label: TextBox as reference implementation of component contract
nodes.norm_label: textbox as reference implementation of component contract

nodes.label: Toast duplicate handling policy
nodes.rationale: Allow (default) always shows a new toast; Block drops a repeat and leaves the existing toast untouched, for when a repeat means nothing new happened; Replace drops the new one but folds it into the existing toast, incrementing Count and restarting its timer, for when the repeat itself is the information the user should see.

nodes.label: Tick-driven pausable countdown
nodes.rationale: The timer is ticked in 100ms increments (TickMilliseconds) rather than awaited as one Task.Delay, so hovering can pause the countdown (toast.Paused) without cancelling it. The CSS progress bar pauses the same way via a CSS custom property, keeping the visual bar and the actual dismiss timer in step.

nodes.label: VetoToastMessage.DeduplicationKey
nodes.rationale: Falls back to a composite of type, title and message when the caller supplies no explicit DeduplicationKey, so unrelated toasts with the same wording but different severity are not treated as duplicates.

nodes.label: Service owns the list, host owns the clock
nodes.rationale: The service deliberately knows nothing about timing or animation: it does not start auto-dismiss timers because the caller's Duration may be null and only the host knows what null means, and it does not remove a leaving toast because only the host knows how long the exit animation runs. This division lets the host resolve host-level defaults centrally while the service stays a pure data/policy store.
nodes.norm_label: service owns the list, host owns the clock

nodes.label: Max-toasts eviction rule
nodes.rationale: When the live (non-leaving) toast count reaches MaxToasts, the oldest non-sticky toasts are retired to make room. Sticky toasts are exempt because they are on screen precisely because they must not disappear on their own.

nodes.label: VetoComponentCore
nodes.rationale: Veto has two base classes (VetoComponentBase and VetoInputBase<TValue>) because a form component must inherit Blazor's InputBase<T> for @bind-Value, EditContext and validation, and C# allows only one base class. Rather than duplicate shared behaviour, both hold a VetoComponentCore instance and delegate to it, so id generation, class building, style building and attribute filtering exist in exactly one place.

nodes.label: VetoEffects
nodes.rationale: Implements the shared glow/ping visual effects once, for the same structural reason as VetoComponentCore: a form component cannot derive from VetoComponentBase, so shared behaviour must live somewhere neither base class owns. Effects render on a pseudo-element of the root, which is why VetoTextBox carries the effect on its wrapper rather than the bare input/img element that cannot host a pseudo-element.

nodes.label: VetoInputBase<TValue>
nodes.rationale: Base class for every Veto form component; inherits Blazor's InputBase<TValue> for @bind-Value, ValueExpression, EditContext and FieldIdentifier. Cannot also derive from VetoComponentBase due to single inheritance, so it implements IVetoComponent and delegates to VetoComponentCore to share behaviour written once.

nodes.label: VetoDashboardLayout
nodes.rationale: A preset assembled from the shell pieces (app bar, drawer, content region) for an admin frame sized for VetoDashboard tiles. Described as a shortcut, not the only way in - VetoLayout should be composed directly when the preset does not expose something needed.

nodes.label: VetoDock
nodes.rationale: Magnification needs the pointer's continuous position rather than merely which item is hovered, so it is computed in JavaScript (veto-dock.js) and applied through a custom property; dropped entirely under reduced motion and for coarse pointers. VetoDockAppearance.Magnified mirrors the macOS dock; Flat mirrors the Windows taskbar. Position, auto-hide and keyboard handling are shared across appearances.

nodes.label: VetoDockItem
nodes.rationale: Renders an anchor when Href is set and a button otherwise so navigation stays navigation. Dock acts as a toolbar: it takes a single tab stop and moves between items with arrow keys rather than requiring tabbing through every icon.

nodes.label: VetoDockLayout
nodes.rationale: A full-bleed page frame with a floating dock over it - a desktop metaphor rather than a document. Dock items are supplied via the Items parameter rather than nested children because the layout owns the dock itself; VetoDock should be composed directly for full positional control.

nodes.label: VetoDocsLayout
nodes.rationale: A documentation frame preset assembled from the shell pieces. The table of contents is hidden below 1280px rather than stacked, because a contents list above the content it describes is considered noise.

nodes.label: VetoAppBar
nodes.rationale: Registers its resolved height on every parameter change (not just once) so VetoLayoutState.AppBarHeight stays correct when the height changes at runtime, keeping the content region's offset accurate.

nodes.label: VetoDrawer
nodes.rationale: Every drawer behaviour (persistent, temporary, mini rail, responsive) ships in one component selected via Variant, rather than the app choosing/writing one. The responsive behaviour is pure CSS - only the open/closed state is tracked in C# - so there is no viewport-width listener, no layout-shift on boot, and it behaves correctly in prerendered HTML before WASM starts. A one-time JS measurement (veto-layout.js matchesMinWidth) closes a responsive drawer that starts open on a narrow viewport, since a drawer defaulting to open would otherwise cover the whole screen on a phone; the stylesheet handles every width change after that.

nodes.label: VetoLayout
nodes.rationale: The root of an app's page frame. Children (VetoAppBar, VetoDrawer, VetoMainContent, VetoFooter) can be placed in any order because the frame positions them via cascaded VetoLayoutState, so markup reads top-to-bottom instead of being nested to match the visual result.

nodes.label: VetoLayoutState
nodes.rationale: Lets shell pieces coordinate without knowing about each other: the drawer registers its width and variant, and the main content reads them to offset itself, even though neither is anywhere near the other in the markup.

nodes.label: VetoMainContent
nodes.rationale: The drawer-anchor class is applied whenever a drawer exists regardless of open state (since it decides which grid column content occupies), while the drawer-variant/breakpoint classes only describe what the drawer is doing - whether that affects layout at a given viewport width is left entirely to CSS media queries, keeping the drawer and content in agreement about breakpoints.

nodes.label: IVetoThemeService
nodes.rationale: Registered by AddVeto() and injectable anywhere so a page can flip the theme without going through a component.

nodes.label: VetoTheme
nodes.rationale: Every property is optional; anything left null keeps the built-in value from VetoStyles.css, so an app rebrands by setting only the tokens it cares about rather than restyling the whole library. Overrides are emitted as CSS custom properties on :root so they cascade into every component, including ones rendered into portals outside the provider's own markup. Token values are regex-guarded against characters that could close a style declaration/rule/element since they are written directly into a <style> block.

nodes.label: VetoThemeProvider
nodes.rationale: Renders no element of its own so it never disturbs a layout. Appearance is carried by the data-veto-theme attribute on <html>, maintained by the service; the component only supplies overrides and triggers re-renders on theme change. JS interop for InitializeAsync is deferred to OnAfterRenderAsync's firstRender because it is unavailable while prerendering.

nodes.label: VetoThemeService
nodes.rationale: Every JS call is guarded because during prerendering there is no browser to talk to; the theme stays at its default until the component renders interactively. OnSystemPreferenceChanged is public only because JS interop requires it via [JSInvokable], not because it is part of the public API.

nodes.label: VetoThemeToggle
nodes.rationale: Uses inline SVG for mode icons rather than an icon-library dependency, because the toggle is often the first Veto component an app renders and should not require choosing an icon set first.

nodes.label: veto-code.js (clipboard interop)
nodes.rationale: copyText returns false rather than throwing when the browser refuses, because the Clipboard API requires a secure context and a user gesture, neither of which is guaranteed.

nodes.label: VetoDock pointer magnification pattern
nodes.rationale: Magnification falls off across neighbouring items based on continuous pointer position, which cannot be expressed in CSS alone; listeners live in JS and write custom properties without crossing into .NET, using a raised-cosine falloff so neighbours look like a wave rather than snapping.

nodes.label: Delegated pointer drag pattern for VetoGantt bars
nodes.rationale: One delegated pointer listener on the grid rather than per-bar handlers, because bars come and go as rows are filtered/collapsed/re-sorted; drag preview is done in JS with a CSS transform and .NET is invoked exactly once on release (OnBarDragged) to avoid dozens of interop round trips per second which would stutter WASM and be worse over a Server circuit.
nodes.norm_label: delegated pointer drag pattern for vetogantt bars

nodes.label: PGlite + localStorage mirrored persistence pattern
nodes.rationale: Tries PGlite (Postgres-in-WASM via IndexedDB) for per-user Gantt edit overrides but always keeps a localStorage mirror underneath: every read/write awaits the same opening promise so a save during PGlite's async load cannot split across stores, and localStorage is written on every save regardless of backend so a slow or blocked CDN never makes edits appear lost. Mirror wins on read when present since it is always the newer of the two; the PGlite table is read only when the mirror was never written.

nodes.label: veto-theme-init.js anti-flash boot script
nodes.rationale: Must be added to <head> as a plain synchronous, non-deferred, non-module script before any stylesheet link, applying the remembered theme before first paint; otherwise a prerendered page renders light then snaps to dark once WASM boots, visible on every navigation.

nodes.label: data-veto-theme attribute (single source of truth for appearance)
nodes.norm_label: data-veto-theme attribute (single source of truth for appearance)

nodes.label: VetoTilt3D pointer-driven compositor animation pattern
nodes.rationale: Pointermove listener lives in JS rather than crossing into .NET because it fires dozens of times a second (costly in WASM, worse over a Server circuit); JS writes two CSS custom properties and CSS/compositor does the transform, so .NET is never involved in the animation.

nodes.label: HandbookContent (Handbook demo content)
nodes.rationale: Body text is deliberately lorem ipsum filler, long enough per section that following a contents-rail anchor visibly moves the page - demonstrating what the contents rail is for.

nodes.label: VetoDocsTheme (docs site brand palette)
nodes.rationale: Red on white in light mode, red on black in dark; primary colour chosen for 6.9:1 contrast on white so it is legible as body-weight text, not just a fill. Danger colour is deliberately darker/cooler than the brand red so error states are not mistaken for an accent; colour never carries meaning alone (also sets aria-invalid and renders a message).

nodes.label: Veto Component Contract (Class/Style/Id/TestId/Visible/AdditionalAttributes)
nodes.rationale: Id auto-generates so for/aria-* never dangle; Class/Style append after the component's own so the consumer always wins; every component exposes the same surface regardless of base class.

nodes.label: VetoInputBase<TValue>
nodes.rationale: Inherits Blazor's InputBase<TValue> to get @bind-Value, ValueExpression, EditContext and FieldIdentifier for free rather than hand-rolling two-way binding.

nodes.label: VetoComponentCore
nodes.rationale: Single implementation both base classes delegate to, so shared behaviour is written once - contract additions go here, not duplicated in both bases.

nodes.label: CssBuilder
nodes.rationale: Never build class strings by concatenation; use CssBuilder for modifier classes like Modifier("sm") -> veto-dock--sm.

nodes.label: Scoped CSS with --veto-* Tokens Only
nodes.rationale: A hard-coded color is a bug: it will not follow the theme. New tokens go in wwwroot/VetoStyles.css when genuinely missing.

nodes.label: Glow / Ping Effects - done
nodes.rationale: Off by default; colour follows the component's role then theme; drawn on a pseudo-element so it never fights a component's own box-shadow; holds still rather than disappearing under reduced motion.

nodes.label: VetoTheme (Palette Model) - done
nodes.rationale: C# palette emitted as inline --veto-* properties, so apps rebrand without editing library CSS.

nodes.label: Anti-flash Boot Script - done
nodes.rationale: Applies stored theme before first paint; without it every prerendered page flashes light.

nodes.label: VetoTilt3D - done
nodes.rationale: Pointer tracked in JS so nothing crosses into .NET per frame; dropped under reduced motion and for coarse pointers.

nodes.label: VetoBreadcrumbs / VetoBreadcrumb - done
nodes.rationale: A step is a link only with Href, text otherwise, or a button when OnItemClick is wired - lets the same component draw a file path or a wizard.

nodes.label: VetoButton - done
nodes.rationale: Renders an anchor when given Href; a disabled button never does, because a disabled anchor still navigates.

nodes.label: VetoSwitch<T> - done
nodes.rationale: Two-state is an ARIA switch; three-state is an ARIA checkbox, the only role whose aria-checked may be mixed.

nodes.label: VetoSlider<T> - done
nodes.rationale: Built on native range inputs so keyboard, touch and pointer capture come from the browser; only the rail, fill and marks are drawn.

nodes.label: VetoRating<T> - done
nodes.rationale: AllowHalf clips a filled copy over an empty one so halves work for every icon rather than only glyphs with a purpose-drawn half.

nodes.label: VetoGantt Drag-to-Reschedule - done
nodes.rationale: Dragging is one delegated pointer handler on the grid, not per-bar, because bars come and go as rows are filtered/collapsed/re-sorted.

nodes.label: PGlite (WASM Postgres persistence)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in, falls back to localStorage; veto-gantt-store.js routes every read and write through one opening promise so edits saved without PGlite loaded aren't lost; open question whether a multi-megabyte WASM Postgres earns its place for a handful of date overrides.

nodes.label: VetoHandbookPage / VetoHandbookToc - done
nodes.rationale: Built from one shared section list so the article and its contents rail cannot disagree.

nodes.label: VetoCode - done
nodes.rationale: Renders code as text so Razor snippets display rather than execute.

nodes.label: VetoBlinkText - done
nodes.rationale: Teletype reveal supporting an IAsyncEnumerable stream input for API or model output.
